briefs.notes: OCCWI Scenario Immersion Protocol (SIP) brief. Structured prevention training methodologies for comand leaders and primary prevention officers, swapping compliance slides for behavioral labs. Prepared for Elizabeth Walther.
briefs.title: Scenario Immersion Protocol (SIP)
briefs.description: An experiential training methodology addressing persistent engagement challenges in prevention education.

structured.throughline: Transitioning prevention training from compliance-oriented lectures to immersive behavioral laboratories.

problem_layer.surface: Persistent engagement challenges and checkbox training fatigue.
problem_layer.deeper: Lecture-based prevention models fail to impact actual behavioral patterns.
problem_layer.structural: A structural reliance on passive slide decks instead of active, scenario-based learning protocols.

structured.path: Deploying active scenario immersion protocols where leaders discover their own behavioral patterns under simulated stress.
structured.purpose: Sustaining Command readiness and reducing prevention risk factors globally.
roadmap: Milestone 1 (Months 1-6): Pilot SIP training units in select environments.
Milestone 2 (Months 6-12): Validate behavioral change metrics using primary feedback loops.
Milestone 3 (Months 12-18): Scale SIP framework across the command structure.

briefs.notes: Operation Babylift community archival project. Translating historical records of separation from the Vietnam War era into collaborative healing and art installations.
briefs.title: Operation Babylift | Separation into Repair

structured.throughline: Translating historical records of wartime separation into collective, community-led acts of repair.

problem_layer.surface: Wartime separation records remain fragmented and inaccessible.
problem_layer.deeper: Standard archiving systems treat personal histories as simple bureaucratic metadata.

structured.path: Assembling open-access community databases and tactile art archives to reconnect historical lineages.

Milestone 3 (Months 12-18): Launch strategic community memorial exhibitions.
